title: Challenges for human oversight in detecting system malfunctions in AI-assisted medical diagnostics
desc: Increasingly, physicians must oversee AI systems to detect system malfunctions. We studied 48 physicians in a randomized controlled study using an increasingly malfunctioning AI for cardiac auscultation. Diagnostic performance declined alongside AI reliability, even when physicians were cognitively forced to make an initial classification, and when human performance exceeded AI reliability. Physicians’ confidence declined faster than their trust in AI. Results call for specification of oversight goals and processes ensuring patient safety.

title: The deep learning framework Hist2Prot infers single-cell spatial proteomics from histology to predict biomarkers and clinical outcomes
desc: Spatial proteomics enables high-resolution mapping of protein expression within the tumor microenvironment, but its routine clinical application remains limited by cost, technical complexity and restricted tissue coverage. Here we present Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework that generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine hematoxylin and eosin histology. Trained on approximately 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset, Hist2Prot was evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets comprising approximately 72 million additional cells, showing concordance with measured protein profiles and outperforming established baselines. Hist2Prot-derived virtual proteins preserved immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and recapitulated clinically relevant tumor microenvironment organization. Across seven independent patient cohorts comprising 1,774 patients, virtual spatial proteomics improved molecular biomarker, prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction beyond hematoxylin and eosin morphology alone. Hist2Prot enables scalable single-cell computational spatial proteomics from routine histology for precision oncology.

title: AI-based prediction of actionable genomic alterations from H&E-stained slides
desc: Precision oncology based on the identification of actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) has been transformative in the care of solid tumors, yet optimal treatment selection is often hindered by tissue exhaustion and slow turnaround times. Artificial intelligence (AI) addresses these barriers by predicting AGAs directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Recent landmark studies, including the prospective EAGLE and ANNAR trials, have demonstrated that deep learning models can identify alterations such as EGFR in non-small cell lung cancer and FGFR in urothelial cancer across diverse global cohorts. By providing near-instant, non-destructive results, AI-based prediction can triage patients for molecular testing or clinical trials at the time of initial diagnosis. This perspective evaluates the maturing evidence base and outlines a pragmatic pathway for integrating these tools into clinical practice. Ultimately, these models offer the opportunity to extract critical molecular information from slides generated in every laboratory worldwide and to significantly improve timely access to the rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape of solid tumors.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven multiple sclerosis diagnosis using genomic and medical imaging data: a review.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated central nervous system condition with heterogeneous clinical manifestations, progressive neurodegeneration, and considerable variability in disease trajectory. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) methods, have improved MS diagnosis and risk prediction. However, comprehensive review studies emphasizing the potential of existing AI-powered MS diagnosis remain limited. Thus, this study investigates the utilization of multimodal data by AI models to enhance diagnostic accuracy, evaluate disease progression, and optimize personalized care strategies. By adhering to PRISMA guidelines, this review included 26 studies encompassing MRI-based analysis, retinal OCT imaging, blood transcriptomics, SNP genotyping, and multimodal clinical datasets. An additional classification of these studies by modality was performed, and they were assessed with respect to dataset size, performance metrics, biomarkers, methodological robustness, and model interpretability. The findings indicate a consistent trend toward outstanding diagnostic performance, with some AI models achieving accuracies exceeding 95% using medical imaging and genomic data. However, limited external validation and interpretability procedures create a gap in clinical applicability and trustworthiness. This review highlights AI's growing potential to revolutionize MS diagnosis.

title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
desc: Structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) models typically treat each clinical concept as a dataset-specific token, discarding the natural-language semantics associated with the event. As a result, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence, without directly exploiting any prior semantic knowledge. We investigate how pretrained causal language models can be adapted for longitudinal EHR prediction by developing tEHR. Here, we represent events with their natural language description and use this text stream to apply EHR-adaptive continued pretraining, followed by task-specific discriminative fine-tuning using LoRA, utilising the LLM as a longitudinal patient-encoder. We evaluate this approach across four prediction tasks on the MIMIC-IV dataset and pancreatic cancer prediction on the CPRD dataset at 1 to 12 month horizons, with tEHR using the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone achieving the strongest overall performance. Ablations show that performance declines when clinical descriptions are removed or misaligned, when numerical values are omitted, and when either stage of adaptation is removed, while explicit elapsed-time descriptions provide little additional benefit. Analysis of the learned patient representations further reveals clinically coherent structure associated with distinct patterns of disease risk and clinical history.

title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
desc: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation. Users with functional disorders generated 1.8 times as many physician escalations and 2.6 times as many laboratory orders as other users, but no more prescriptions. This profile differs from the younger, predominantly female populations reported for direct-to-consumer telemedicine. It moves chronic disease management, functional disorder pathways, and care coordination from aspirations to design requirements, and we argue that deployed AI care platforms should characterize their populations against national benchmarks early.

title: Bloom unifies brain cell representations across modalities and contexts
desc: Multimodal genomic datasets now profile mammalian brain cells across anatomical regions, developmental stages, disease states, and species. Learning shared representations that capture cellular diversity across these heterogeneous observations remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce Bloom, a transformer-based model that represents cells using gene expression, chromatin accessibility, or both. Bloom is trained on 300,000 adult mouse brain cells with paired measurements, randomly sampled with broad-subclass balancing--approximately 100-fold fewer cells than used by comparable pre-trained models. By combining genomic sequence embeddings with randomly sampled multimodal cell views, Bloom outperforms unimodal cell models in resolving brain-wide cell types and in annotation, regression, and label-transfer tasks. Its attention patterns reveal cell-type-dependent associations among genomic loci, including pairs separated by millions of base pairs. These results establish Bloom as a data-efficient framework for integrating multimodal brain cell measurements and generating hypotheses about cell-type-specific genomic relationships.

Enhanced skin tone and blood estimation through AI-enabled upscaling of discrete reflectance spectra
desc: Objective quantification of epidermal melanin content and dermal blood volume is crucial for equitable applications in dermatology and in the evaluation and engineering of optical devices, such as pulse oximeters, where variable amounts of melanin may introduce inaccuracies. Here, we demonstrate a method leveraging diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and a machine-learning framework using fully connected neural networks (FCNNs) to non-invasively estimate melanin and blood indices from sparse data through spectral upscaling. We validated the algorithm on custom phantoms, porcine skin, and in vivo human participants. In phantoms with variable blood and melanin (0–20%), the model achieved high accuracy (R2 > 0.90) to absolute concentrations. In porcine skin, estimated melanin strongly correlated with histology-derived density scores (Pearson r = 0.95). Across six regions of the human hand, the FCNN accurately estimated pigmentation from sparse wavelengths, even during hand-raise challenges that induce confounding blood volume changes. After upscaling, sparse-wavelength estimates strongly correlated with a model using over 450 wavelengths (Pearson r = 0.96), reducing data requirements ~ 150-fold without compromising accuracy. These findings highlight the importance of high-spectral information for disentangling melanin and blood contributions in reflectance spectra and the capacity of machine-learning to restore predictive performance from sparse inputs. These findings demonstrate that artificial-intelligence -driven spectral upscaling can enhance objective skin tone quantification in wearable optical devices.

title: Sepsis in 2026: from bundles to biology. A critical review.
source: PubMed · Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
desc: [Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia] Sepsis remains associated with a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite more than two decades of Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) recommendations. The 2026 update reinforces early recognition, resuscitation, timely antimicrobial therapy, source control, and reassessment, yet the benefit of increasingly intensive implementation of standardized measures may be approaching a ceiling. A central limitation is treating sepsis as a homogeneous entity despite the wide variation in etiologies, host susceptibility, immune responses, and clinical trajectories. Artificial intelligence, host-response biomarkers, rapid microbiological diagnosis, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic optimization provide new opportunities to shorten the time to effective intervention. In parallel, transcriptomic, genomic, and routine clinical data can identify subphenotypes and endotypes associated with different prognoses and potentially different treatment responses. Secondary analyses of clinical trials illustrate how an intervention that is neutral overall may be beneficial in biologically defined subgroups. The next step should combine SSC bundles with biological stratification, adaptive trial designs, and point-of-care tools capable of matching treatment to patient profile in real time. This review proposes a transition from standardized sepsis management toward precision medicine: the right treatment for the right patient at the right time.

title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
desc: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, drug feature data, and treatment response measurements. Using these data, we retrained and evaluated multiple publicly available DRP models under three model-building scenarios: training models using cell line data only, training models using combined cell line and PDO data, and pretraining models on cell line data followed by fine-tuning on PDO data. We then evaluated and compared model prediction performance on PDOs across these analysis scenarios. In addition, we also assessed the consistency of drug screening viability data generated by different laboratories using different assay technologies and/or experimental protocols.

title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
desc: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-ExperimentAssay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccinerelated study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Cryo-EM/ET Particle Classification
desc: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is widely used to determine protein structures from purified samples. With cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET), it is possible to image thin sections of cells and directly visualize diverse proteins in their native environment. However, separating the massive mixture of different types of proteins inside cells remains challenging, especially without human intervention. In this work, we present an unsupervised deep learning framework for classifying cryo-EM/ET particle images that jointly optimizes for pose and structure through an autoencoder-based multi-stage pipeline. On single-particle cryo-EM datasets, our framework can capture the continuous variation in particle views and separate images of real particles from contamination. Using in silico mixtures of multiple types of proteins, we demonstrated our method's capability of separating the protein classes without supervision. Finally in a real cryo-ET dataset of algal chloroplast, our deep learning model successfully detected the four main protein complexes of photosynthesis on native thylakoid membranes. Taken together, these results demonstrate that our framework offers a scalable, annotation-free solution for robust structural discovery across diverse cryo-EM and cryo-ET applications.

Multicenter benchmarking of large language models for bladder cancer management recommendations from mpMRI reports
desc: Large language models (LLMs) can interpret radiology reports, but their ability to generate guideline-concordant recommendations from bladder cancer multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) reports remains uncertain. Following TRIPOD-LLM, we retrospectively evaluated nine API-accessed LLMs using 590 mpMRI reports from three hospitals under two input conditions: original Chinese reports and clinician-translated, quality-controlled English reports. Two physicians independently rated each model-generated recommendation on a 1–5 ordinal scale. We analyzed 21,240 ratings using patient-level random-intercept cumulative link mixed models, with paired Wilcoxon tests as secondary exploratory analyses. The association between input condition and physician rating differed across LLMs (likelihood-ratio chi-square = 683.05, df = 8, P < 0.001). Compared with original Chinese input, clinician-translated English input was associated with higher ratings for chatgpt-o3-pro (OR 2.79, 95% CI 2.29–3.41), deepseek-v4-flash (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.19–1.81), claude-opus-4-7 (OR 3.07, 95% CI 2.47–3.82), and gpt-5.5 (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.53–2.32), but with lower ratings for claude-sonnet-4-5 (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.36; all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Four LLMs showed no clear input-condition difference. Center-specific contrasts also depended on input condition and were materially unchanged after adjustment for age, sex, pathological T stage, tumor grade, tumor number, and maximum lesion diameter. Inter-rater agreement was substantial (quadratic weighted kappa range, 0.621–0.743). Readability did not track physician-rated recommendation quality. These findings argue against clinician-translated English as a universal optimization strategy and support model-specific validation of input conditions before clinical deployment. LLM-generated recommendations from mpMRI reports are best positioned as clinician-supervised, imaging-based decision support rather than standalone treatment advice.

title: Unsupervised AI-assisted self-medication: a cross-sectional survey.
source: PubMed · Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
desc: [Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy] Self-medication is common worldwide and increasingly informed by artificial intelligence (AI) tools, but their intersection is understudied, particularly in conflict-affected settings such as Syria. To assess self-medication among adults living in Syria and their use of AI tools for medication-related information. An online cross-sectional survey of 255 adults (22 February-7 March 2026) assessed self-medication, AI use, trust, pharmacist-AI preferences, and privacy awareness. Analyses comprised descriptive statistics, chi-square tests with Cramér's V, and exploratory principal component analysis (PCA; n = 86 complete cases) with a sensitivity analysis (n = 149). Self-medication was reported by 80.8% of respondents, without a sex difference (p = 0.579), and 30.6% used antibiotics without prescription. AI tools were used for health queries by 61.6% (ChatGPT by 45.5% of all respondents), more often by younger (p = 0.002) and more educated respondents (p < 0.001). Among AI users, 66.2% asked medication-related questions, 68.2% trusted AI information conditionally, and 59.2% preferred pharmacists; in 16 of 17 disagreements, the pharmacist's advice was followed. PCA identified self-medication intensity, health literacy, and AI engagement components; the first two were reproduced in the sensitivity analysis, whereas a weak link between adverse drug reactions and AI engagement was not. In this digitally connected sample, AI-assisted health information seeking was common and coexisted with frequent self-medication and non-prescribed antibiotic use. These cross-sectional associations support digital health literacy initiatives, safeguards within AI platforms, and pharmacist engagement with AI-informed patients.

title: Curiosity-0826-4B: Generative Medical Event Sequence Modeling Across Pediatric and Adult Populations
desc: We introduce Curiosity-0826-4B, an updated version of the generative medical event foundation model trained on Epic Cosmos that simulates patient timelines to produce zero-shot clinical predictions. Curiosity-0826-4B incorporates a broader patient population and richer clinical event representations, while generally matching or exceeding Curiosity-0226-1B, the largest model in the previous Curiosity-0226 series, on evaluated tasks supported by both models. Laboratory value prediction improved, with MAE 18--46% lower than that of Curiosity-0226-1B. We evaluated prediction of disease events across pediatric cohorts aged 2--17 years. AUROCs for new asthma diagnosis (0.742--0.785) and asthma exacerbation (0.829--0.852) were comparable to those in the adult reference cohort, while AUROCs for sickle cell crisis (0.820--0.847) were lower than in adults (0.915). Explicit representation of documented death enabled new mortality prediction tasks among adults across hospice, inpatient, and ambulatory settings (AUROC 0.821--0.942). Scaling-law analysis guided compute-optimal initial pretraining followed by continued pretraining with context extension. The resulting Curiosity-0826-4B model has more parameters (4.3B versus 1B) and a longer context window (16K versus 8K). It processes 56% fewer training tokens and requires 2.2 times the training floating point operations (FLOPs) compared with its predecessor. By extending a common zero-shot prediction strategy to pediatric patients and additional outcomes, Curiosity-0826-4B broadens opportunities to develop clinical and operational applications without training separate task-specific models. Further validation should assess local calibration, performance across patient subgroups and event frequencies, timeline completion rates, and generalization to new settings, alongside prospective evaluation of clinical and operational utility.

title: BenchmarkHub: an open-source platform for reproducible evaluation of large language models in healthcare
desc: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are solely judged by their scores on biomedical benchmarks, yet these scores are rarely reproducible since the prompts, inference settings and model builds are seldom reported. We developed BenchmarkHub, an open-source platform for auditable evaluation of language and vision-language models for biomedical research. Methods: BenchmarkHub is a Python web application (Django 5.2, SQLite) released under the MIT licence and available at https://github.com/juanjuanignacio/benchmarkhub. The application can be accessed through a browser interface, a set of command-line tools and a REST API, so interactive exploration and scripted pipelines produce identical, comparable records. The platform samples questions with fixed seeds, runs models directly or as tool-using agents in a code sandbox, grades answers with deterministic rules and stores every prompt, reply and tool call. The interface provides a leaderboard to rank performance of the models, allowing model comparison without any preexisting programming knowledge. Findings: We used BenchmarkHub to evaluate 12 open-weight models in five experiments on 15 biomedical benchmarks (11 text, two multimodal and two computational biology) and two general benchmarks. The pooled accuracy ranged from 46.1% (95% CI 43.0-49.3) to 80.9% (78.3-83.3). Re-grading the responses with simple answer-extraction rules lowered a model's accuracy by up to 33.1 percentage points, leading to a reorder of the leaderboard. Published scores were found for 23 out of the 143 benchmark/model combinations tested. The accuracy measured by BenchmarkHub was lower than in the published results in 19 out of the 23 available comparisons. The effect of four prompting protocols (1: default prompt; 2: asking the model to answer the letter only; 3: chain-of-thought prompting; 4: three-shot prompting) changed MedQA accuracy by up to 11.3 points but was not significant after multiple-testing correction with 150 questions. We also tested the impact of ablation on benchmarking using the MMMU benchmark dataset. Removing images lowered the accuracy by 18.0 and 19.3 points respectively for the two strongest models. Finally, the accuracy of agentic benchmarks using a sandboxed interpreter increased on computational biology tasks by 36-63 points. title: HieraPTM: From PTM Site Recognition to Functional Phosphosite Prediction through Hierarchical Context and Protein Mechanics
desc: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate cellular signaling and protein function, making accurate site identification essential for understanding protein regulation. However, PTM site recognition and functional phosphosite prediction are largely modeled independently, limiting the transfer of large-scale recognition knowledge to functional prioritization. Here, we introduce HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos, a cross-task hierarchical framework that separately models and conditionally integrates transferable PTM recognition representations and function-specific mechanical evidence. HieraPTM integrates local sequence patterns, protein language model representations, and three-dimensional structural information to recognize multiple PTM types. HieraFuncPhos transfers these representations through parameter-efficient adaptation and adaptively retrieves local and distal mechanical evidence conditioned on functional representations. At HSP90AA1 T36 and T115, the model reveals distinct mechanical response patterns consistent with published nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observations, suggesting that the framework not only prioritizes functional phosphosites but also provides biophysically grounded, testable hypotheses regarding site-specific regulation. HieraPTM achieved macro-averaged AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.9237 and 0.8425 across eight PTM tasks, while maintaining competitive performance on severely imbalanced external benchmarks. HieraFuncPhos achieved an AUROC of 0.8274 and an AUPRC of 0.8188, outperforming existing comparison methods. Together, this framework connects PTM site recognition, functional prioritization, and structure-informed hypotheses regarding potential regulatory processes.

Artificial Intelligence in Inpatient Medicine: Skills for the Hospital Physician.
desc: [Clinical medicine (London, England)] Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from novelty to daily use in internal medicine: ambient documentation, point-of-care literature synthesis and diagnostic support are already in routine use. This review describes the skills needed to use these tools safely: critical appraisal of the evidence behind a tool, oversight of generated documents against the source record, verification of factual claims, calibration of trust to demonstrated reliability, and lawful handling of identifiable patient data. We summarise the drivers of adoption, the measured benefits, the characteristic failure modes, and how physicians can acquire these skills through continuing professional development.

title: Constructing and Validating Memorisation Audits for EHR Foundation Models
desc: Autoregressive electronic health record (EHR) foundation models may disclose training information at inference, yet clinical predictability makes patient-specific memorisation difficult to distinguish from generalisation. We evaluate fixed-window token reconstruction, sensitive-attribute disclosure, and random patient-level canaries in GPT-2-style models trained on MIMIC-IV, across early, best-validation, and final checkpoints. Reconstruction improves with additional context, but training--held-out differences remain small. Trajectory-unique prompts containing limited clinical information produce no excess sensitive disclosure for training patients. In a matched model with random binary patient-level canaries, training-patient label-recovery AUROC increases from 0.512 to 0.549 while held-out recovery remains at chance. An overfit 1,000-patient positive control achieves near-perfect recovery, confirming sensitivity to strong memorisation. These results reveal weak cohort-level memorisation but no reliable patient-level disclosure under the evaluated attacks. They motivate clinically grounded inference-time audits that can detect patient-specific memorisation in existing models without retraining with canaries.

title: Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning for Uncertainty-Robust Multi-Label Chest X-ray Classification
desc: Background: Automated multi-label classification of chest radiographs is complicated by overlapping imaging findings, noisy report-derived labels, and changes in disease co-occurrence across clinical settings. Existing clinical-hierarchy methods can encode label relationships, but a rigid hierarchy may conflate categorical membership with empirical association and propagate annotation errors. Methods: We investigated Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning (ReCaRL), a graph-assisted framework for multi-label chest radiograph classification. An image encoder produces initial finding scores, while a graph constructed from training-label associations provides reliability-weighted, confidence-gated updates. Uncertain annotations are handled with observation masks. The evaluation compares flat, weighted, graph-based, and hierarchy-penalty baselines, with internal and external discrimination and calibration assessments. Results: In the internal evaluation, ReCaRL achieved macro AUROC 0.821 and macro AUPRC 0.437, compared with 0.812 and 0.423 for the masked/weighted baseline. Mean AUROC across five common findings was 0.865 versus 0.858. External testing yielded AUROC 0.799 and AUPRC 0.409. Post-hoc calibration reduced the internal Brier score from 0.113 to 0.102 and the external expected calibration error from 0.082 to 0.061, without changing AUROC or AUPRC. Conclusions: Reliability-aware graph propagation and confidence gating were associated with modest improvements in multi-label chest radiograph classification relative to the matched masked/weighted baseline. Post-hoc calibration improved probability reliability in the reported evaluations. The findings do not establish a benefit in prospective clinical decision-making.

title: ModBERT: a DNA modification and genetic variant-aware DNA large language model
desc: The development of foundation models that learn a general grammar of DNA (DNA language models) has accelerated in recent years. The vast majority of DNA large language models (LLMs), such as DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, are pretrained almost exclusively on reference genomes. They therefore cannot represent the two sources of variation most directly tied to regulatory differences between people: genetic variants and DNA methylation. Long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) now measures both from the same native DNA molecules, but no model is designed to use this joint readout. With this in mind, we developed ModBERT, a DNA language model built on a five-letter probabilistic genome representation in which each position is a distribution over A, C, G, T, 5mC (represented with M). In pretraining, these distributions encode population allele frequencies and CpG methylation levels from 242 individuals in the 1000 Genomes Long-Read Sequencing Consortium, learned with a soft-target masked language modeling objective. We further propose probabilistic fine-tuning, in which the same representation encodes one individual's genotype and methylation. A fine-tuned model can then make person-specific predictions from a single assay. Under this novel fine-tuning framework, we show that ModBERT effectively utilizes methylation information to classify peaks from functional genomic assays, including histone mark (n=11 different marks) and transcription factor binding (n=69 TFs) ChIP-seq data, outperforming ab initio trained models and ModBERT pretrained on sequences without methylation. In silico methylation perturbations yield TF sensitivities that correlate with independent methylation-aware motif models. Using an evaluation design that separates generalization to new loci from generalization to new individuals, ModBERT predicts chromatin accessibility at held-out loci in held-out individuals (AUROC 0.88). Its predicted variant effects agree with likely causal caQTLs (Spearman correlation = 0.52) but not with variants associated only through linkage, a traditionally challenging task. Overall, ModBERT establishes a framework for personal-genome language modeling, in which a model reads each individual's genetic and epigenetic sequence rather than a shared reference. Self-reported artificial intelligence use, knowledge, and perceptions among undergraduate medical students at a Peruvian university.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in medical education, yet evidence regarding its actual use, knowledge, and perceptions among undergraduate medical students in Peru remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of self-reported AI use for academic activities and to describe patterns of use, self-reported knowledge, and perceptions among undergraduate medical students at a Peruvian university, with an exploratory assessment of associated characteristics. We conducted an observational, analytical, cross-sectional study in 2024 among students enrolled at Universidad Ricardo Palma. A total of 279 responses were received; one respondent did not provide informed consent and was excluded, leaving 278 participants for analysis. Data were collected using an adapted online questionnaire based on previously published instruments. AI use was assessed through a separate yes/no question regarding previous use of any AI tool. Overall, 257 of 278 participants (92.4%) reported previous AI use for academic activities. Most participants self-reported basic knowledge of AI principles (89.2%) and awareness of its use in medicine (95.3%). Among the predefined AI-tool categories, ChatGPT (69.1%) and Canva (19.8%) were the most frequently reported. The primary contribution of this study is descriptive, documenting the prevalence and patterns of AI use, self-reported knowledge, and perceptions in the surveyed population. Secondary exploratory regression analyses suggested associations with daily digital-device use and perceptions regarding treatment planning, but these estimates should be interpreted cautiously because only 21 participants were classified as non-users. These findings highlight the need for structured education addressing critical, ethical, and responsible AI use in undergraduate medical training.

title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation
desc: Recent advancements in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLM) enhance X-ray report generation, but often neglect clinical context, overlook workflow integration, and lack explainability, which hinders clinical adoption due to interpretability and reliability concerns. This paper addresses the dual challenges of performance and expert explainability in automated X-ray report generation for clinical AI applications. Our proposed approach, TransXplainRRG, utilises an off-the-shelf Swin Transformer model along with a transformer-based text encoder that incorporates patient medical history to generate a radiology report. Further, we explore an expert-guided `inside-out' approach and extract only abnormal findings for radiology report refinement. Thus, this study bridges the gap between high-performance automation and interpretability critical for clinical practice by combining state-of-the-art transformer-based vision encoders, text encoders, and LLMs. TransXplainRRG is trained and tested on the large-scale MIMIC-CXR dataset and further evaluated on the unseen IU X-Ray dataset to demonstrate its generalizability and robustness. We employed the GREEN metric as a complementary measure of clinical consistency, achieving scores of 0.327 on MIMIC-CXR and 0.605 on IU X-Ray, both higher than those achieved by MAIRA-2 under the same evaluation setting. It also performed competitively across standard evaluation metrics, frequently matching or surpassing state-of-the-art models. Additionally, we introduce qualitative evaluation metrics developed from radiologists' viewpoints and conduct a preliminary radiologist evaluation on 100 generated reports to assess their clinical relevance. Quantitative and qualitative analyses further demonstrate the potential of our TransXplainRRG framework for reliable and explainable radiology report generation.

title: Spatial multi-omic profiling of non-autonomous transcriptomic and epigenomic responses to genetic perturbation
desc: Multicellular organisms develop and maintain differentiated cell states through a combination of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, including signal transduction pathways mediated by ligands, receptors, and kinases. Genetic perturbation through CRISPR pooled screening is widely used to study cell-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, but the challenges of cellular-resolution in situ measurement have limited the study of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms. We developed Perturb-Tags, a spatial multi-omic technique for pooled CRISPR screening that tags nuclei with spatial barcodes, allowing joint measurement of single-nucleus gene expression, CRISPR guide RNAs, chromatin accessibility, and spatial positions within intact tissue. Perturb-Tags achieves cellular-resolution, unbiased gene expression and multi-omic profiling, and higher sensitivity than previous spatial perturbation approaches. We used Perturb-Tags to systematically perturb ligands, receptors, and all expressed kinases in human embryoid bodies. These experiments revealed extensive non-autonomous gene expression changes after perturbation, including distance-dependent loss of signaling pathway activity upon ligand knockdown, compensatory upregulation of alternative signaling pathways, and responses to receptor and kinase knockdown that vary with cell microenvironment. We also identified changes in the spatial organization of cells with ligand and kinase knockdowns. Finally, we trained a graph neural network to model the combined effects of genetic perturbations on gene expression and chromatin accessibility across an entire tissue. Our work provides a powerful experimental and computational platform for mechanistic studies of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms across healthy and diseased tissues.

title: 外媒聚焦中国医疗AI重估！《福布斯》深度剖析德适科技：iMed-6.0包揽国际双榜冠亚军，对标美股Tempus AI
Machine learning-based experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors.
source: PubMed · Physics in medicine and biology
desc: [Physics in medicine and biology] Objective. Scintillation detectors with excellent timing resolution enable more precise localization of radiation sources in positron emission tomography, leading to substantial improvements in diagnostic capability for diseases such as cancer and dementia. At the timing precision required for such applications at the picosecond scale, detector performance is governed by the dynamics of scintillation photons generated within the detector and their subsequent detection processes. However, detector signals have conventionally been treated only as collective responses of many photons due to structural constraints inherent to photodetectors. In this study, we overcome this fundamental limitation using deep learning framework.Approach. The proposed method estimates photon-by-photon arrival times directly from detector waveforms without requiring any modification to the detector structure; the method operates on an event-by-event basis without ground-truth labels by integrating an unsupervised learning framework with a physically informed detector-response model.Main results. Through comprehensive validation combining Monte Carlo simulation and experimental measurements across various detector configurations, we experimentally demonstrate improved timing resolution, visualized depth-of-interaction-dependent photon transport, and classified Cherenkov and scintillation photons based on the estimated photon-level timing information using a unified deep learning-based framework.Significance. These results provide experimental access to photon dynamics, bridging the gap between theoretical modeling and experimental observation, and they open a new data-driven pathway for discovery in detector physics and optimization.

title: Fine-Tuned Small Language Model for Synthetic Clinical Data Generation and Predictive Healthcare Analytics
desc: The reduced availability of medical datasets represents an important challenge in the development of predictive models for remote healthcare solutions, especially when the available data are imbalanced or difficult to extend through traditional methods. Small Language Models (SLMs) have become a promising alternative to Large Language Models (LLMs) for addressing these limitations due to their lower computational requirements and adaptability to specialized tasks. However, their performance remains highly dependent on the quality and representativeness of the available training data. In this paper, we propose a method for clinical data augmentation based on a fine-tuned Microsoft Phi-2 model that is used to generate synthetic instances, with the purpose of improving deep learning-based model for predicting remotely monitored vital signs. The Phi-2 model was adapted to the medical domain through supervised fine-tuning on the MedQuad dataset, through a Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA)-based method and by applying few-shot prompting techniques. The resulting model was used afterwards in the augmentation of a small-sized dataset, composed of vital sign values and labels associated with pathological and physiological states. The experimental results demonstrate that fine-tuned SLMs improved the performance on medical domain, achieving higher scores for both lexical (ROUGE) and semantic (BERTScore) evaluation metrics compared to the pretrained model. Moreover, the fine-tuned SLM is effective for generating structured synthetic clinical data. When used for data augmentation, the generated dataset improved the performance of a LSTM predictive model, increasing the classification accuracy from 89.0% to 93.7% and showing consistent improvements in precision, recall, and F1-score.

title: Affinity-guided design of PDZ-binding peptides in a shared latent space
desc: PDZ-binding motifs (PBMs) are short C-terminal sequences that bind PDZ domains and contribute to protein localization and complex assembly. Designing PBMs could modulate these interactions while leaving most of the original protein sequence unchanged. Because PDZ recognition preferences overlap, modulating intended interactions requires considering off-target binding alongside target affinity. Computational PBM design methods generally use sequence-based affinity prediction and structure-based evaluation, but it remains challenging to guide sequence searches toward different binding objectives with a single trained model. Here, we propose a deep learning-based method to design PBMs by analytically formulating single-target, off-target-aware, and dual-target design objectives as directions in a PDZ-PBM shared latent space learned through quantitative PDZ-PBM affinity prediction. In single-target PBM redesign for DLG4-PDZ3, our method identified 100 top-ranked candidates, 84 of which were in the top 1% for experimentally measured interaction fitness in a published mutant library, compared with 64 using an existing method. In single-target de novo design of 10-residue PBMs, our method achieved the highest median in silico binding scores among the compared methods for three of the four PDZ domains tested. In off-target-aware and dual-target PBM design for PTPN3 and SCRIB-PDZ3, off-target-aware design increased between-group score differences within each domain at the cost of lower target-domain scores, whereas dual-target design yielded scores close to those of the respective single-target designs for both domains. Together, these results show that shared latent representations learned from quantitative affinities allow a single trained model to guide PBM design across different binding objectives without retraining.

title: 心玮医疗携手思脉德医疗与爱思科技达成战略合作，共建医疗AI
Benchmarking general and medical LLM performance in Parkinson's disease management.
desc: [Clinical parkinsonism & related disorders] Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as clinical support tools, yet their performance in Parkinson's disease (PD) management remains insufficiently characterized. We evaluated a general-purpose LLM (Gemini 1.5 Pro) and a medically specialized LLM (OpenEvidence) using 45 synthetic PD vignettes requiring generative assessment and management recommendations. Responses were independently rated by two movement disorders fellows using predefined 5-point Likert scales, with adjudication by a senior specialist when required. Both models demonstrated generally good performance in clinical assessment, whereas management recommendations were less reliable. A modest numerical advantage was observed for the medically specialized model across assessment, plan, and composite outcomes, although no statistically significant differences were identified. Qualitative analysis showed that clinically relevant errors occurred in both models, predominantly reflecting treatment strategy errors. These findings suggest that, in the specific model versions evaluated, LLMs may support clinical reasoning in PD, but require cautious interpretation, particularly for treatment recommendations.

title: Physics-based simulation unlocks scaling laws for generalizable MRI reconstruction
desc: Deep-learning-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction holds great promise for accelerating acquisitions, yet its clinical translation remains bottlenecked by poor generalizability across unseen scanners, populations, anatomies, and protocols. Gathering sufficiently diverse clinical datasets to overcome this bottleneck is hindered by high acquisition costs, privacy restrictions, and institutional biases. Here, we introduce Scalable Inverse Model (SIM), a framework that systematically co-designs physics-simulated training data, model architecture, and learning paradigms around scalability--leveraging compute scaling to overcome historical data bottlenecks and achieve robust zero-shot MRI reconstruction. Across 14 public and in-house datasets--spanning seven international centers, five vendors, field strengths of 0.3-7 T, over ten anatomical regions, more than ten acquisition protocols, downstream quantitative and molecular tasks, and a 150-scan blinded radiologist study--SIM demonstrates robust zero-shot generalizability, recovering fine anatomical details while suppressing aliasing artifacts where conventional deep-learning methods fail. Attention-map analyses confirm that SIM learns physically explainable, dynamically adaptive reconstruction primitives rather than anatomy-specific priors. SIM establishes a scalable, privacy-preserving, and democratized infrastructure for universal MRI reconstruction, providing a blueprint for generalizable AI across inverse problems in medical imaging.

title: 中国AI突破复杂肺癌诊疗！中美医疗圈集体坐不住了
Facilitating Patient Education Using Intraoral Scan Superimposition.
source: PubMed · Compendium of continuing education in dentistry (Jamesburg, N.J. : 1995)
desc: [Compendium of continuing education in dentistry (Jamesburg, N.J. : 1995)] This article highlights the use of intraoral scan (IOS) superimposition as a visual tool for dental professionals to educate patients regarding their soft-tissue condition. In a representative case, eight IOS were captured and superimposed using a patient monitoring system in which the software overlays new IOS over previous scans using artificial intelligence comparison tools ("Difference Map," "Comparison Slider," and "Cross Section"), providing a longitudinal visual record of both morphological and color changes in the gingiva. Chairside visualization of the treatment progress served as an effective educational tool, reinforcing oral hygiene habits to supplement successful disease management.

title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
desc: We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. It searches for the lowest target for which a bolus and constant infusion keep the predicted probability of at least one MAP reading below 65 mmHg after the rise phase within a prescribed limit. If no such target is found, the decision returns to the clinician. We assess calibration of the predicted minimum MAP on retrospective surgical records under the doses actually administered. In a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients, the method recommended a dose for 74 % of patients at a nominal risk of 5 %. Among the patients receiving a recommendation, 6.9 % had a reading below 65 mmHg. A fixed target of 70 mmHg yielded a rate of 25 % when applied to the full virtual cohort.

title: DHP 2026汇聚海外收入占比超过90%的医疗人工智能公司，共同探讨韩国医疗保健全球扩张战略。
Greater mental health use and concern about Generative AI among college students with anxiety-depression.
source: PubMed · Journal of American college health : J of ACH
desc: [Journal of American college health : J of ACH] Objective: To examine whether generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use and AI-related sentiment differ across anxiety-depression symptom groups among college students. Participants: 890 U.S. college students who completed the elective AI module of the 2024-2025 Healthy Minds Study. Methods: Participants were grouped into Anxiety-Depression, Anxiety Only, Depression Only, and Neither using GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores (≥10). ANCOVAs with Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons examined AI use (overall, mental health, companionship) and AI-related sentiment, adjusting for sociodemographic covariates. Results: Overall AI use did not differ across groups. Mental health-related and companionship AI use differed across groups; the Anxiety-Depression group reported greater mental health-related use than the Neither group (p < .01). The Anxiety-Depression group also reported greater concern about AI than the Neither group (p < .01). Conclusions: Differences across anxiety and depression symptom groups were evident for specific forms of GenAI use and AI-related concern, but not for overall use.

title: Beyond Binary Classification: Multiclass Machine Learning for Diabetes and Prediabetes Risk Prediction Using NHANES
desc: Detecting diabetes risk early is important for preventing disease progression. Most existing machine learning approaches focus on binary classification, which limits their ability to capture intermediate risk states such as prediabetes. We develop a supervised learning framework to classify adults as normal, prediabetic, or diabetic using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data. The framework uses routinely collected demographic, clinical, and lifestyle variables from 15,356 adults, with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) used only to define labels and excluded from input features to prevent leakage. We compare conventional machine learning and transformer-based models and examine two binary formulations: normal versus prediabetes, and normal versus combined prediabetes and diabetes. Models are evaluated on a held-out test set using precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. In the multiclass setting, performance is broadly consistent across models, with accuracy up to 0.72 and macro-averaged F1 of 0.70. Prediabetes remains the most challenging class, with F1 scores of 0.54 to 0.56 for conventional models and 0.53 to 0.55 for transformers, reflecting its overlap with both neighboring states. When the task is reduced to normal versus prediabetes, F1 scores rise modestly to 0.62 to 0.64. A more substantial improvement is observed under a broader screening formulation combining prediabetes and diabetes, with F1 scores of 0.73 to 0.74 across all models. These findings suggest that feature overlap along the biological continuum between normal and diabetic states contributes more to the difficulty of prediabetes detection than model architecture. Multiclass prediction provides a more clinically informative representation of metabolic risk progression but highlights a trade-off between clinically meaningful stratification and predictive accuracy.

title: Deep learning detection and biological interpretation of arterial stiffness from retinal fundus images in diabetes.
desc: [iScience] Pulse wave velocity is the gold standard for assessing arterial stiffness (AS) but is costly and not widely accessible. This multicenter study developed a deep learning model to predict AS from fundus images. Trained on 64,440 images from 36,412 adults with diabetes at China's National Metabolic Management Centers and externally validated on 6,217 images from two independent hospitals, the model achieved an AUC of 0.780 (95% CI: 0.769-0.792) and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754-0.790) in internal and external validation, respectively, outperforming models using classical risk factors alone. The fusion model integrating fundus images with clinical factors significantly improved test-set performance (AUC = 0.853, 95% CI: 0.844-0.863) and demonstrated good external generalizability (AUC = 0.801, 95% CI: 0.784-0.816). Ablation studies indicated retinal arteries were associated with AS, with other retinal structures also contributing. These findings support deep-learning-based fundus-image analysis for AS screening in real-world clinical settings, and retinal-structure analyses for exploring AS pathophysiology.

title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
desc: This paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture for AI (EAAI), a conceptual framework treating Data, Information, Knowledge, Understanding and Wisdom as five distinct but recursively interacting epistemic functions: observation, contextual interpretation, modeling and prediction, critical evaluation and informed judgment. Two observations motivate it: sequential readings of the Knowledge Pyramid obscure how these functions interact, and a targeted review of ten Bayesian reference books finds that prior distributions are defined mathematically while "prior information" and "prior knowledge" are not consistently distinguished as epistemic categories. A Bayesian interpretation relates the likelihood, prior and posterior distributions, posterior prediction, model checking and decision analysis to the five functions, without limiting EAAI to Bayesian systems. Extending "prior" in an epistemic sense, the paper distinguishes five kinds of prior context that can shape the model, the likelihood, the prior, evaluation and action. Three worked applications -- quantitative financial risk, actuarial modeling in health insurance and agentic AI for medical reimbursement claims -- show how EAAI structures the analysis of model assumptions, evidence interpretation, validation, dependencies and decision consequences, separating the prediction of a risk, the appraisal of its reliability and the justification of action. It draws implications for AI and machine learning, including evaluation by function, treating intermediate model outputs as evidence open to challenge and separating generation from appraisal, and compares EAAI with work on DIKW, Bayesian workflow, AI evaluation and risk governance. Its contributions are an epistemic vocabulary with recursive relationships, a more accessible reading of Bayesian methodology, a typology of prior context and clearer methodological terminology.

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
source: PubMed · Journal of computational biology : a journal of computational molecular cell biology
desc: [Journal of computational biology : a journal of computational molecular cell biology] Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
desc: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly used to automate biomedical research, creating a growing need to benchmark their capabilities on real scientific data and workflows. Their reliability in neuroimaging remains insufficiently characterized, where plausible analytical outputs can conceal errors that affect scientific conclusions. Existing studies have advanced scientific question answering and tool-based automation, but provide limited evidence on workflow reconstruction, acquisition of procedural expertise and evidence-based scientific judgment. Here we present NIBench, a neuroimaging benchmark comprising three complementary evaluations of autonomous agents. First, we benchmark execution and workflow reconstruction using 56 tasks across seven tool ecosystems, covering structural, diffusion and functional magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and multimodal analyses. Second, we examine whether agents can evolve their procedural skills through distillation of execution trajectories, evaluating the resulting skills on previously encountered tasks, unseen tasks and other models. Third, we assess scientific judgment using 36 claims from published Alzheimer's disease studies, requiring agents to analyse raw cohort data and provide reproducible evidence. We evaluate 19 language models within a shared agent framework, with selected models undergoing skill distillation and claim evaluation. Leading agents execute supplied analysis protocols nearly perfectly, whereas withholding procedural guidance widens performance differences. Distilled skills improve performance on acquisition tasks and transfer between models, but benefits on unseen tasks are inconsistent. Agents reproduce their reported results yet sometimes reach conclusions inconsistent with expert-derived answers, and access to data does not always improve judgment.

title: MOF Nanozyme Sensor Array Encodes Wavelength-Resolved Catalytic Fingerprints for Interpretable Pesticide Screening.
desc: [ACS sensors] Rapid pesticide screening is limited by low-dimensional optical readouts that may not preserve sufficient information to distinguish structurally diverse residues and estimate their concentrations. Here, three poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP)-modulated MOF-199 copper nanozymes were combined with laccase-like, peroxidase-like, and superoxide dismutase-like chromogenic reactions to construct a 3 × 3 cross-reactive material-reaction sensor array. Quantitative XPS and N2 sorption revealed PVP-dependent differences in surface composition, external surface area, and pore volume. Across eight pesticides and twelve concentrations from 0.1 to 100 μg mL-1, full UV-vis spectra from 400 to 700 nm were assembled into 9 × 301 matrices. A multitask one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) decoded these matrices to jointly perform pesticide classification and concentration regression, achieving 94.4% accuracy, macro-F1 = 94.4%, R2 = 0.894, and RMSE = 10.46 μg mL-1 in standard-solution tests. Spectral-window ablation showed improved prediction with broader wavelength coverage, while an endpoint comparison further supported the advantage of the full spectral representation. Input-gradient and Grad-CAM analyses mapped model reliance to material-reaction channels and chromogenic wavelength regions, supporting interpretable identity-concentration decoding. In apple, cucumber, and pepper matrices, the trained nine-class classifier assigned representative pesticides and blank controls with 97.2% overall accuracy. These results demonstrate that wavelength-resolved catalytic fingerprints support interpretable classification and concentration estimation of single-pesticide samples in standard solutions and retain class-discriminating information in the tested produce matrices.

title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification
desc: Local Binary Patterns (LBP) remain among the most widely used texture descriptors, from industrial inspection to medical imaging. Yet their radius, sampling angles, color transform and thresholds are fixed by hand for each dataset. We present FLEX-LBP, which learns these parameters by backpropagation while every forward pass computes exact binary codes and hard histogram counts. A straight-through estimator acts only in the backward pass, so the deployed descriptor is an interpretable hard-binary LBP with 90 learnable parameters and unchanged inference cost. In a controlled ablation on six color texture benchmarks, the component worth learning is dataset-dependent. One configuration, applied unchanged everywhere, learns the geometry and thresholds with the color transform frozen. It improves the nearest-neighbor accuracy of the identical fixed descriptor by 3.55 points on average over five seeds, significantly on five of six benchmarks and never significantly worse. With a linear discriminant readout, it gains 0.9 points; the fully learned descriptor gains 2.7 and has the highest mean. FLEX-LBP is more accurate than five classical LBP-family descriptors, PCANet and a neural LBP on five of six benchmarks. Its mean nearest-neighbor accuracy exceeds that of frozen ImageNet ResNet-50 features (23.5 million parameters). On the Kather colorectal cancer histology benchmark, the fully learned descriptor reaches 93.8%, significantly above the best classical descriptor (Completed LBP, 92.8%). The learned radii adapt in directions that recur across seeds. Noise drowns single-pixel comparisons and illuminant change flips inter-channel ones; median sampling or gray-world normalization restores 96-97%. The code is available as a drop-in PyTorch layer at https://github.com/medalimoussa/FLEX-LBP.

title: Learning to Navigate a Changing World: From Brain Systems to Novel Algorithms.
source: PubMed · The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
desc: [The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience] Natural organisms navigate a world in constant flux and are frequently confronted with sensory ambiguity and shifting goals. While biological systems can adapt rapidly to navigate in novel and nonstationary environments, this challenge remains a significant hurdle for artificial intelligence. In this review, we examine recent progress in understanding neurobiological systems that allow for adaptive, efficient spatial and abstract navigation in dynamic environments and how these observations have informed new developments for the same behavior in machines. We highlight how predictive learning serves as a unifying framework to describe the organization of neural activity across distributed systems for navigation, including the hippocampal formation, parietal cortex, and higher-order associative structures. Specifically, we explore how such neurobiological systems encode expected future states, dynamic target trajectories, action plans, and internal behavioral strategies. Finally, we contrast the diffuse, inefficient exploration of canonical artificial agents with the structured, efficient control policies for goal-directed navigation observed in natural organisms. By grounding learning in the interplay between action, prediction, and natural behavioral statistics, navigation provides a roadmap for building resilient, neurobiologically inspired continual learning in artificial agents.

title: TuMAP: A Dual-View, Morphotype-Aware Pathomics Pipeline for Quantifying Renal Tubular Remodeling
desc: Quantifying disease-associated renal tubular remodeling is challenging because tubular appearances are heterogeneous. We introduce TuMAP (Tubular Morphotype-Aware Pathomics), a pipeline combining (1) dual-view foundation-model representations and provisional morphotype annotation, (2) compositional and within-morphotype pathomics, and (3) patient-level statistical inference. From 456,158 tubules in 358 PAS-stained kidney biopsy slides, TuMAP identified eight image-based morphotypes, seven of which showed stable subsampling assignments. Across 219 patients in six diagnostic groups, diabetic nephropathy (DN) and tubulointerstitial nephritis/acute tubular injury (TIN/ATI) each differed from minimal change disease in seven morphotype proportions, while IgA nephropathy differed in six. DN showed reduced nuclear solidity and increased eccentricity across all eight morphotypes. Area-normalized nuclear density exposed additional within-morphotype differences. TuMAP provides a framework for separating changes in tubular morphotype composition from phenotypic differences within morphotypes.

title: Beyond the Rogue Agent-Preparing Health Systems for AI Failure.
